clue.text: Cannon ball receiving name given by soldiers

indicators.note: 'given by' places the soldiers' letters next to the rest, here in front of them

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword term for ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: the dance word takes the name's letter into itself, so it is the container here

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A cannonball gets a nickname from the troops who fire it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cannon ball' reads as one object, but 'Cannon' alone is the definition; 'receiving' gives DNANCE, the ball word holding the name letter, and 'given by' sets the soldiers in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance is the collective term for artillery, of which a cannon is the classic example.

clue.text: Inaccurate opening score

explanation.surface: An inaccurate first score in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Missing the target means wide or inaccurate; getting a first run in cricket is to open one's scoring.

clue.text: Strong drink — grounds to abandon car in middle of road?

definitions.text: abandon car in middle of road?

parts.note: a double is a two-measure serving of spirits, a strong drink
a park is grounds, as of a stately home

explanation.surface: Drinking spirits and then leaving the car in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. The definition is playful: a double-parked car sits outside a parked one, out in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Double-parking leaves a car alongside one already parked at the kerb, blocking the carriageway.

clue.text: Book review

parts.note: not a critique of a novel but an official inspection of a firm's account books

explanation.definitionFit: An audit is a formal examination of an organisation's financial records, a review of its books.

clue.text: Piano recital's taken

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Piano recital's taken (7,5)': recital gives CONCERT, but no clue word gives GRAND; a word such as 'thousand' seems lost in OCR and no search found the full text.

clue.text: Child holding woman's an angel

indicators.note: the child word holds the woman's word inside it, so 'holding' is the container signal

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, and also a junior scout, so a child
her is the possessive used for a woman

explanation.surface: A small child with a woman is behaving like an angel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an angel' looks like praise for the child, but it is the definition; the child is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a winged heavenly being, often painted as a chubby child, one of the orders of angels.

clue.text: Seriously hamper group taking on maths problem

indicators.note: the group takes on the muddled letters ahead of itself
a problem with the maths letters means they are muddled into a new order

parts.note: a ring is a group, as of conspirators

explanation.surface: A team struggling with a maths problem is badly held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges the maths letters into HAMST, and 'taking on' sets that ahead of the group word.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamstring someone is to cripple their efforts, from cutting a tendon behind the knee.

clue.text: Register and get moving

explanation.surface: Signing in and setting off.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll is a list of names such as a school register; to roll is to start moving, as cameras or a car do.

clue.text: Play in the street

parts.note: not children at play but a musician performing outdoors for passers-by's coins

explanation.definitionFit: Busking is performing music in public places for money from passers-by.

clue.text: Establishing waif's short of money

indicators.note: 'short of' says the waif word lacks something, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a foundling is an abandoned child, a waif
L stands for the pound, from Latin libra, a unit of money

explanation.surface: Setting up a home for an abandoned child is held back for lack of funds.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of waif's is 'is'; 'short of' drops L from FOUNDLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Founding an institution means setting it up, establishing it for the first time.

clue.text: Underwear from shopping area aboard

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Underwear from shopping area aboard (6)': SMALLS is MALL inside SS, but 'aboard' must both give SS (on a steamship) and signal the container, one word doing two jobs.

clue.text: On behalf of the country, maintaining university press

indicators.note: the phrase keeps the university letter inside it, so 'maintaining' signals a container

parts.note: for the state means on behalf of the nation

explanation.surface: A university's publishing house works on behalf of the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maintaining' puts U inside FOR THE STATE. 'press' looks like a university press, but it is journalism.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth estate is a traditional name for the press and journalists, after the three estates of the realm.

clue.text: Be only temporary garrison commander?

parts.note: a stand-in in charge of a stronghold until relief arrives is minding the defences for a while, the idiom for keeping things going in someone's absence

explanation.surface: A soldier is left briefly in charge of a garrison.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means to keep things running while someone is away; the clue reads it literally as a stopgap commander of a fort.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to cope or keep things going until someone returns, pictured as a stand-in garrison commander.

clue.text: One discarded out of hand that may give you the slip

definitions.text: One discarded out of hand that may give you the slip

parts.words: One discarded out of hand that may give you the slip
parts.note: a hand is a bunch of bananas; the peel thrown away from one is the classic thing to slip on

explanation.surface: Something rejected without a thought that lets someone escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of hand' reads as 'without thought', but a hand is also a cluster of bananas; 'give you the slip' means escape but here literally make you slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded fruit peel is the comic cause of a fall, and figuratively any blunder that trips someone up.

clue.text: Deceive about salary date

indicators.note: 'about' means the letters of salary date are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Lying to someone over when they will be paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' scrambles SALARY DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone astray is to mislead them, to deceive or corrupt them.

clue.text: In the sea, work conveyor

indicators.note: 'In the sea' puts the work word inside the sea word

parts.note: the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone working out at sea is ferrying goods across it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conveyor' suggests a belt in a factory, but it is a light-hearted definition: a moped carries its rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A moped is a small motorbike, a vehicle that carries a rider from place to place.

clue.text: See animal sprint round house, in fact

indicators.note: 'in fact' puts the earlier letters inside the fact word

parts.note: a deed is a thing done, a fact, as in 'in deed and word'

indicators.note: the sprint word goes round the house abbreviation

parts.note: to run is to sprint

explanation.surface: Watch a beast dash around a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link pointing to the animal. 'round' gives RHOUN, the sprint word around the house letters, and 'in' puts that inside the fact word.
explanation.definitionFit: A deerhound is a large rough-coated hunting dog, an animal.

clue.text: Meet train for a change, as one may at King's Cross

definitions.text: as one may at King's Cross

indicators.note: 'for a change' asks for the letters of the two words to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Meeting a train for once, as a passenger might at a London station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' scrambles MEET and TRAIN. King's Cross is a London terminus, where trains end their journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Trains finish their runs at a terminus such as King's Cross, so to end there is what the clue describes.

clue.text: Element to make electrically safe, by choice

indicators.note: 'by' sets the choice word beside the other, here in front of it

parts.note: rare means exceptional, of choice quality
to earth a circuit is to connect it to the ground so it is safe

explanation.surface: Wiring something safely according to your own preference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' puts RARE beside EARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare earths are a group of metallic elements such as lanthanum and cerium, so one is a chemical element.

clue.text: To hold United, pull back defender

indicators.note: 'To hold' says the pulled-back word takes the United letter inside it
'pull back' reads the pull word backwards

parts.note: to drag something is to pull it
U is the usual abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A football team pulls back a defender to keep hold of their lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DRAG into GARD, and 'To hold' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard protects someone or something, so is a defender; in sport too a guard is a defensive player.

clue.text: Pass traffic lights, indicating with these?

parts.note: to hand something over is to pass it
traffic lights are road signals

explanation.surface: A driver goes through the lights, signalling by arm as they do so.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole picture: drivers once indicated by arm, the way a cyclist still does.
explanation.definitionFit: Arm gestures given by cyclists or drivers to show a turn are the means of indicating the definition describes.

clue.text: Obstruct smooth progress, as mug?

parts.note: read as an instruction, the answer says to write the word gum upwards, which in a down light spells this word

explanation.surface: Getting in the way, like a fool would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as mug?' is a reverse clue: GUM written UP, from the bottom of a down light, reads MUG.
explanation.definitionFit: To gum up machinery is to clog it, stopping it running smoothly.

clue.text: Fighting man at first should expect such a reception?

definitions.text: Fighting man at first should expect such a reception?

parts.note: war is fighting between nations

indicators.note: 'at first' takes only the opening letter of man

explanation.surface: A soldier going to war should expect a hot welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives M from 'man'. A warm reception is a hearty welcome, and for a soldier under fire, a hot one.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm reception is a friendly welcome, or, ironically, a hostile one with heavy fire.

clue.text: Something in the kitchen to drink

explanation.surface: Something to drink in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A sink is a basin for washing up in a kitchen; to sink a pint is to drink it down.

clue.text: As physician, I must conceal ill feeling

indicators.note: 'conceal' says the answer is tucked away inside the run of words physician, I must

explanation.surface: A doctor must keep their hostility to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is a link; 'conceal' hides the answer in physiciAN I MUSt.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is hostility or ill will towards someone.

clue.text: having riotous time?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'having riotous time? (8)' is cut short at the start: the definition of HAYMAKER is missing, and no search found the full text.

clue.text: Emperor rejecting Kipling's work? Bother!

indicators.note: rejecting the novel turns its title back to front

parts.note: Kim is Rudyard Kipling's novel
ado means fuss or bother

explanation.surface: An emperor scorns a Kipling novel as a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns KIM into MIK. The question mark hints that the Mikado is itself a work, by Gilbert and Sullivan.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikado is an old title for the Emperor of Japan.

clue.text: Wielded, could it offer any power?

definitions.text: Wielded, could it offer any power?

indicators.note: wielded means swung about, so the words any power are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether arms, once wielded, really give anyone power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wielded' scrambles ANY POWER; the whole clue also describes arms, which give power when wielded.
explanation.definitionFit: Weapons collectively are wielded and are the means by which force or power is exerted.
